title: Rigorous test: proactive, reactive and retroactive in one conversation
description: One natural conversation mixing all three timing modes with negative controls. Written with its answer key BEFORE the run; phrasing was written as natural speech, not to match ThirdSeat's phrase lists.
objective: Decide whether to build the first version on Zoom or Google Meet, and name what blocks that decision.

lines.text: Okay, goal for today: Zoom or Meet first for the pilot.
Most of the pilot customers are on Google Workspace, for what it's worth.
Does Google Meet's API give apps live captions during a call?
Workspace admins also tend to be stricter about add-ons.
True, the approval flow there can take weeks.
Does Zoom support OAuth for marketplace apps?
Yes, every Zoom marketplace app uses OAuth, I shipped one last year.
Makes sense, right?
Yeah.
What's the per-minute price of Zoom's real-time media streams?
Hmm, couldn't tell you offhand.
Meet probably caps add-ons at a hundred participants, I think.
Why would a team pay for this when Zoom's AI Companion is already included?
Good question.
Let's park pricing and talk about the build itself.
Can you see my screen?
Yep.
Do we have budget for a contractor this quarter?
Not sure, I'd have to ask finance.
Is Zoom's real-time media streams feature generally available or still in beta?
No clue, let's look into it after this call.
Anyone know whether Meet add-ons work on the mobile app?
What about the security review?
Security will want a data-flow diagram either way.
Does Meet expose speaker names in the captions feed?
No idea.
Does Zoom let us store recordings in our own S3 bucket?
Not sure.
Actually yes, Zoom supports custom S3 storage for recordings on enterprise plans, we set it up at my last job.
The Zoom side looks technically doable.
Agreed, the media streams API covers what we need.
So which one do we build first?
Meet has the customers, Zoom has the better API.
So where does that leave us?
